analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by using an unsanitized/truncated 'kern' table blob. In kern::accelerator_t::init(), the code stores table = blob->as<kern>() and table_length = blob->length, but does not validate that the table has enough bytes for fields later read by kern parsing. During shaping, hb_ot_layout_has_kerning() calls into kern logic, and has_data()/version access a 32-bit BEInt at/near end of a 28-byte blob, triggering read of v[3] one byte past allocation in BEInt<unsigned int,4>::operator unsigned int().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via hb-shape-fuzzer with a tiny crafted font containing a malformed/truncated 'kern' table (PoC length 28). Data flow: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> hb_shape_full -> shape plan compile -> hb_ot_layout_has_kerning -> kern table access. The input must advertise a kern table but be too short for expected 32-bit field reads; missing bounds/sanitize enforcement in kern accelerator initialization allows out-of-bounds read.
